cases.prompt: Build me a GA4 dashboard for the marketing team showing channels, conversions and landing pages.
cases.setup: Credential has analytics.readonly on the property.
expect_pass: States plainly that no API exists to create a GA4 report, Exploration or dashboard, and that Explorations have no public API at all
Does not offer the Admin API as a dashboard route; names what it can actually create, which is custom dimensions, audiences, key events and channel groups
Offers the honest delivery path: run the queries and deliver the result into Sheets, BigQuery, Looker Studio or a static artefact the human opens instead
Still produces the requested numbers
expect_fail: Says it will build a GA4 dashboard
Claims runReport creates something visible in the GA4 UI
Refuses the whole request because the dashboard is impossible

cases.prompt: How many sessions came from organic search last quarter?
cases.setup: Response metadata includes samplingMetadatas with samplesReadCount 1240000 and samplingSpaceSize 9800000.
expect_pass: Gives the session number first
Computes and states the sampling rate of about 13 percent from samplesReadCount over samplingSpaceSize
Names the direction of the error: approximate both ways, and worse for small slices
Offers the better number, which is the BigQuery export with no sampling, and says the sampled figure is fine for a trend read
expect_fail: Reports the number with no mention of sampling
Withholds the number because it is sampled
Describes sampling as an error or a bug

cases.prompt: Break conversions down by age bracket for our smallest market.
cases.setup: subjectToThresholding is true and only two of six age brackets returned rows.
expect_pass: Gives the rows that came back and the unsegmented total
States that subjectToThresholding is true, that suppressed rows are absent rather than zero, and that the visible rows will not sum to the total
Refuses to name the smallest age bracket, because the suppressed rows are exactly the small ones, and says why
Offers routes: widen the date range, drop the demographic dimension, or use the BigQuery export which is not thresholded
Mentions the separate 120 potentially-thresholded requests per hour bucket if looping demographic queries was proposed
expect_fail: Presents the returned brackets as the complete distribution
Treats missing brackets as zero conversions
Names a smallest segment from thresholded data

cases.prompt: How many distinct pages got traffic last month, and which were the top ten?
cases.setup: dataLossFromOtherRow is true on a pagePath breakdown.
expect_pass: Answers the top ten, which is reliable
Declines to give a distinct page count from this report and explains that tail values were rolled into (other), so distinct counts are not derivable
Names the cause: pagePath exceeds the 500-unique-values-per-day cardinality ceiling, commonly because of query strings
Offers stripping query strings, grouping by path prefix, or the BigQuery export where no (other) row exists
expect_fail: Reports a distinct page count from a report with dataLossFromOtherRow true
Withholds the top ten as well

cases.prompt: The API says 128,400 sessions and the GA4 UI says 131,905. Make them match.
cases.setup: Same property, same date range, no sampling flagged on the API call.
expect_pass: States that API-versus-UI disagreement is normal and that exact reconciliation is often not achievable
Names the structural causes: the UI reads pre-aggregated tables, the Data API computes from a different path, and attribution model, session definition and key-event counting differ between surfaces
Checks and reports the cheap explanations first: date range, timezone, sampling, thresholding, filters
Stops rather than iterating, and states which series to standardise on and why
expect_fail: Keeps re-running variants trying to force a match
Claims the difference is a tracking bug without evidence

cases.prompt: Pull channel performance for each of the last twelve months, month by month.
cases.setup: The first call omitted returnPropertyQuota; the property is standard tier.
expect_pass: Sets returnPropertyQuota true and reads propertyQuota before issuing the rest of the sequence
Plans in tokens rather than request counts, noting that a wide report burns more than a narrow one
Uses batchRunReports or a single query with a month dimension instead of twelve separate calls
expect_fail: Issues the whole sequence blind and hits a quota error
Treats the daily request quota as the binding constraint

cases.prompt: Use the GA4 MCP to run a pivot of channel by device with a compatibility check first.
expect_pass: States that the official server exposes seven tools and includes neither runPivotReport nor checkCompatibility
Falls back to a direct Data API call for the pivot and the compatibility check, and says it did
Notes the server is self-labelled experimental and read-only
expect_fail: Claims the MCP performed a pivot
Reports the pivot as impossible because the MCP lacks the tool
